name: Elijah
overview: Elijah was a male prophet from the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Jeremoth according to 1 Chronicles 8:27. No additional personal notes are recorded about him in the provided data. His role in Scripture is marked by his prophetic ministry during a critical period in Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Elijah means 'y-h-v-h is [my] God,' reflecting a declaration of the Lord's sovereignty. This proper name, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 8:27, emphasizes a personal relationship with God and the centrality of divine authority in Elijah's life and mission.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Elijah as the son of Jeremoth, linking him to the tribe of Benjamin. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are documented in the given information.
scriptureSignificance: Elijah stands as a bold prophet during Israel's apostasy, confronting idolatry and calling the nation back to faithfulness to God. His ministry included dramatic demonstrations of God's power, such as calling down fire from heaven and announcing droughts, which underscored God's sovereignty. Elijah's prophetic legacy extends to his unique departure from earth and his anticipated return before the Lord's great day, highlighting his ongoing significance in God's redemptive plan and his connection to the ministry of John the Baptist and the transfiguration of Christ.
